title: A proper morphism is finite near every finite fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $s\in S$. If $f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism] and the underlying set $f^{-1}(\{s\})$ is finite, then there is an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq S$ of $s$ such that the restriction $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. No Noetherian hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

mathlib_searches.query: A proper morphism with finite fibre at a point is finite over an open neighbourhood of that point
For a proper scheme morphism the locus in the target over which it is finite contains every point with a finite fibre
A proper morphism of schemes with finite fibre over s is finite on some open neighbourhood of s

from.place: Temkin §4.2, Lemmas 4.2.1--4.2.2: the finite Gamma_0 set of residual-transcendence-degree-one fibre-generic centres over closed points; Lemma 4.2.1: obtain an actual finite neighbourhood of a fibre-generic point, then use normality to identify the finite birational morphism
